title: The Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, let $\mathfrak U=\{U_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering, and let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal C$. There is a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}=\check H^p(\mathfrak U,\underline H^q(F))\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F),
$$

where $\underline H^q(F)$ is the presheaf $V\mapsto H^q(V,F)$ and $\check H^p(\mathfrak U,-)$ is Cech cohomology with respect to the covering $\mathfrak U$.

proof.text: In the enough-injectives, equal-universe case choose I = injectiveResolution F, and construct the actual double complex D = cechResolutionDoubleComplex I X pi. The construction is termwise Cech followed by flipping the indices, not an existential black box. The independent-universe statement remains open.

For each q use cechResolutionDoubleComplex_columns I X pi q to obtain the column complex isomorphism. For each n use cechResolutionDoubleComplex_total I X pi hpi n to obtain the total homology isomorphism. These two comparisons give exists_cechDoubleComplex by pairing the witnesses.

Apply the first double-complex spectral sequence. Compose its E2 isomorphisms with homology of the column-complex isomorphisms, and transport the abutment along the total homology isomorphisms. This proves exists_cechToDerivedSpectralSequence_of_enoughInjectives. The general HasExt^w statement is still sorry and retains the original double-complex plan, including the required universe comparison.
